package_info.why_malicious: This package is a trojanized version of the legitimate Tor Browser, distributed through unofficial channels such as spam campaigns and Pastebin links. It is specifically designed to steal cryptocurrency by intercepting or exfiltrating wallet credentials and transaction data from users, violating user privacy and security.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user launches the trojanized Tor Browser
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the main Tor Browser executable or bundled scripts (e.g., browser startup scripts or modified core binaries)
required_permissions: filesystem (to access wallet files or clipboard)
network (to exfiltrate data to attacker-controlled servers)

malicious_snippets.code_language: Pseudocode (actual implementation may be in JavaScript, C++, or Python depending on Tor Browser internals)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code monitors for cryptocurrency wallet activity, intercepts wallet credentials or transaction data, and exfiltrates this information to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in theft of cryptocurrency.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code actively monitors for cryptocurrency wallet activity and exfiltrates sensitive credentials or transaction data to external servers. Legitimate browsers do not contain logic to detect, access, or transmit wallet information, making this behavior highly indicative of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal Tor Browser build should not contain any code that accesses, monitors, or exfiltrates user wallet data. The presence of such code violates user trust, privacy, and the expected security guarantees of the Tor Browser.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security tools may monitor wallet activity to alert users of suspicious access, but they do not exfiltrate credentials or transaction data. Legitimate software never transmits sensitive wallet information to untrusted third parties.
key_indicators: Code that hooks or monitors for wallet-related activity (e.g., file access to known wallet paths, clipboard monitoring for wallet addresses)
Network requests from the browser process to attacker-controlled infrastructure outside the Tor network
Exfiltration of sensitive data such as wallet credentials or transaction information
Modification or injection of scripts into browser startup routines

attack_chain.action: Victim is lured to download the trojanized Tor Browser via spam or Pastebin links.
Victim installs and launches the trojanized Tor Browser.
Malicious code monitors for cryptocurrency wallet activity and intercepts credentials or transaction data.
Stolen wallet credentials and transaction data are sent to attacker-controlled servers.

behavioral_signatures: Browser process making unexpected outbound connections to non-Tor, non-update servers
Access to local wallet files (e.g., known wallet file paths for Bitcoin, Ethereum, etc.) or clipboard monitoring for wallet addresses
Injection or modification of browser startup scripts to intercept sensitive data
Unusual process behavior such as reading or copying wallet files immediately after browser launch
file_indicators: Tor Browser executables or installers with mismatched or invalid digital signatures compared to official releases
Presence of additional scripts or binaries not found in official Tor Browser distributions (e.g., extra DLLs, modified startup scripts)
Altered browser core files (e.g., browser.exe, firefox.exe) with hash mismatches
network_indicators: Outbound connections from the browser process to attacker-controlled C2 domains or IP addresses not associated with the Tor network or official update servers
Unusual POST requests containing wallet or credential data in the payload
Connections to hardcoded IP addresses or domains listed in the report as C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Tor Browser installations with mismatched hashes or invalid digital signatures compared to official releases. Detect browser processes accessing known wallet file paths or monitoring the clipboard for wallet addresses. Alert on outbound network connections from browser processes to suspicious domains or IPs not associated with the Tor network. Use behavioral analysis to flag browsers that attempt to exfiltrate sensitive data, and correlate file, process, and network indicators for comprehensive detection.
